LESSON: READING 1.2.1 READING FOR COMPREHENSION

Grade: Grade 8
Subject: INDIGENOUS LANGUAGES
Strand: Strand 1
Topic 1.2: Reading 1.2.1 Reading for comprehension

SECTION 1: WELCOME

• Today’s class: Reading 1.2.1 Reading for comprehension
• How we learn: Teach → Worked example → Try this
• Use point notes. Show working. Then take the quiz.
• Big question: How can we differentiate between actions done in the past and in the present?

SECTION 2: WHAT YOU WILL LEARN

1. answer questions from texts related to the theme for comprehension
2. use the vocabulary on the theme to construct sentences in appropriate tenses for communication

SECTION 3: CLASS STUDY (TEACH → EXAMPLE → TRY)

▸ Reading 1.2.1 Reading for comprehension

• Listen to a model.
• Study the example.
• Then produce your own example.

▸ Reading 1.2.1 Reading for comprehension

Teach
• Focus skill: answer questions from texts related to the theme for comprehension.
• Use complete sentences.
• Speak clearly; write neatly.

Worked example
• Model sentence 1 about Reading 1.2.1 Reading for comprehension.
• Model sentence 2 using a Kenyan school example.
• Model dialogue: A: “…?”  B: “…”

Try this
• Write 5 original sentences on this skill.
• Say one 30-second oral example to a partner.


SECTION: QUICK EXAMPLES

• One clear model for Reading 1.2.1 Reading for comprehension
• One Kenyan school/home example

SECTION: PRACTICE NOW

1. Write 5 sentences.
2. Do one oral practice with a partner.
3. Correct spelling/punctuation.

SECTION: WORK TO DO

1. Revision sheet: meaning + 5 examples + 5 practice items.

SECTION: THINK ABOUT IT

1. How can we differentiate between actions done in the past and in the present?
2. Why is it important to apply comprehension skills in reading?

SECTION: REMEMBER

• Model first, then try.
• Use complete sentences.

• Next: complete the Revision Quiz. Open Answers only after you finish.

— CBC Learn · Classroom study notes (Strategy 2)
